channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Ben Gvir convinced: Likud wants to form a government with Eisenkot
item.description: Otzma Yehudit chairman Itamar Ben Gvir warns that Likud could join forces with Gadi Eisenkot, but stresses: "My only candidate for prime minister is Netanyahu."

item.title: IDF to conduct military exercise in Dead Sea hotel area on Monday
item.description:
A military exercise will take place Monday morning in the Dead Sea hotel area, within the Tamar and Megilot Regional Councils.
During the exercise, increased activity by security forces and military vehicles is expected in the area, and gunfire and explosions will be heard.

item.title: Watch: Footage shows deadly Houthi missile strike on Riyadh airport
item.description: Watch: Footage shows deadly Houthi missile strike on Riyadh airport

item.title: IDF: Terrorist who crossed Yellow Line in southern Gaza eliminated
item.description:
IDF forces operating in the southern Gaza Strip identified a terrorist earlier on Sunday who crossed the Yellow Line and, according to the military, posed an immediate threat.
The forces eliminated the terrorist shortly after identifying him.

item.title: Bennett's statement sparks backlash within opposition
item.description: Together chairman Naftali Bennett says Netanyahu could serve as a minister in his government if he accepts his party's principles. Eisenkot and Liberman reject the idea.

item.title: Shas lawmaker demands Jewish teachers for Jewish school
item.description: Shas lawmaker demands Jewish teachers for Jewish school

item.title: A firing squad for Hasan will encourage Jihadi terror
item.description: For “self-sacrificing" terrorist enemies, nothing could be more fulfilling than the publicity and eternal fame conferred by a US firing squad. Opinion.

item.title: Israel approves Board of Peace team to disarm Hamas
item.description: Israel approves Board of Peace team to disarm Hamas

item.title: ‘The pain remains’: Rabbi who lost daughter, and son in battle, speaks of grief and faith
item.description: Rabbi David Ben Pinchas, who lost his daughter in a car accident and his son in battle in Rafah, speaks about grief, his son’s heroism and faith that remains unshaken: “The pain remains, but it does not affect my faith."

item.title: How Israel and its Arab neighbors can choke Iran's Iraqi proxies
item.description: Baghdad goes through the motions of pushing disarmament deadlines into the distant future, but Iranian officials have made it clear that their proxies are in Iraq to stay. Things can be done to make that a untenable for Iraq. Opinion.

item.title: Kan News poll: Right-wing bloc gains strength, Ben Gvir wins nine seats
item.description:
A poll conducted by the Kantar Institute and published by Kan News found that if elections were held today, Yashar would win 22 seats, the Likud 20, Beyachad (Together) 12, and Otzma Yehudit 9.
Read More

item.title: Samaria security officials arrested in pre-dawn raid
item.description: Two security officials were arrested in a dramatic early-morning operation and barred from meeting their lawyers as a court extends their detention.

item.title: Netanyahu: 'Launch investigation on participants in the film “Naza."
item.description: Netanyahu calls on IDF Chief of Staff, Shin Bet chief, and Attorney General to launch investigation on participants in the film “Naza."

item.title: Two-year-old girl dies after being struck by car in northern Israel
item.description: A two-year-old girl who was critically injured after being struck by a car in Bu'eine Nujeidat has died at Poriya Medical Center.

item.title: IDF: Interceptor launched at suspicious aerial target in southern Lebanon
item.description:
An interceptor was launched a short time ago at a suspicious aerial target identified in an area of southern Lebanon where IDF forces are operating. The results of the interception are being investigated.
No alerts were activated, in accordance with policy.

item.title: Ten injured in accident at Givat Koah Junction
item.description:
A 42-year-old man and a four-year-old boy were moderately injured, and eight others sustained minor injuries in an accident on Route 444 at Givat Koah Junction.
MDA teams treated the injured and evacuated them to Beilinson Hospital in Petah Tikva and Sheba Medical Center at Tel Hashomer.

item.title: Knesset Speaker urges pardon after Netanyahu trial revelation
item.description: Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana appealed to President Isaac Herzog on Sunday, urging him to grant Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a pardon following former Attorney General Avichai Mandelblit’s testimony in Netanyahu’s trial.

item.title: Court extends detention of Samaria security personnel by four days
item.description: The Petah Tikva Magistrate’s Court has extended by four days the detention of two security personnel from Samaria suspected of involvement in a violent incident near Aqraba.

item.title: Polish foreign minister: Man arrested for plotting attack against prime minister
item.description: Polish foreign minister: Man arrested for plotting attack against prime minister

item.title: Lead suspect admits to stabbing Yamano Zalka
item.description: The main defendant in the murder of 15-year-old Yamanu Zalka admitted stabbing him in the leg, but argued he did not foresee the fatal outcome.

item.title: Hospital by day, terror site by night
item.description: The IDF released footage and intelligence indicating that Hamas is continuing to keep the Kamal Adwan Hospital in Jabaliya fully operational.

item.title: Hitler Mussolini wins Peru election
item.description: A candidate named Hitler Mussolini Simeón Flores has won a mayoral election in Peru by just 25 votes. He is not the first person with a name associated with Nazi Germany to win elected office in recent years.

item.title: Arkia expands US-Israel flights: 'You can count on us'
item.description: With daily flights between New York and Israel except Shabbat, expanded aircraft capacity, kosher meals, and a new JetBlue agreement, Arkia is offering travelers greater flexibility and connectivity.

item.title: Netanyahu condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh airport: ‘Terror targets innocent people’
item.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, saying: “Terror targets innocent people and seeks to spread fear. It must be confronted with determination."
Netanyahu added: “Israel looks forward to a strong Middle East - one that stands united against threats, protects its people, and builds a future of security, cooperation, and prosperity for all the peoples of our region."

item.title: Trump: Russia and Ukraine to stop attacking each other’s energy facilities
item.description: US President Donald Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine would stop attacking each other’s energy facilities, warning both sides: “Do not violate the agreement."

item.title: IDF eliminates October 7 Kissufim outpost raid commander in Gaza
item.description: The IDF eliminated a Hamas Nukhba commander who helped lead the October 7 massacre on the Kissufim outpost and participated in abducting Israelis.

item.title: Who leaked info? Yahalomi affair escalates: Suspected invasion of privacy
item.description: Israel’s Privacy Protection Authority has ordered a police inquiry after private messages, AI searches and financial information about Mali and Liel Yahalomi were leaked.

item.title: 42.2 km of longing: Bereaved family members run in Chicago Marathon
item.description: 25 bereaved family members and fellow runners take part in the Chicago Marathon, running in memory of loved ones. The team left Israel on October 7, three years after the massacre, following months of joint training.

item.title: Smotrich: Election may put Hesder yeshiva funding at risk
item.description: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich warns that a change of government could threaten yeshivas, religious institutions and Jewish communities in Judea and Samaria.

item.title: Mysterious cave found in central Israel
item.description: Digging tools found in a cave near Rosh HaAyin. The IDF ruled out a tunnel but circumstances surrounding the excavation are still under investigation.
